findings.claim: A and B cannot be assembled as drawn. The cap screws onto the crown's M26 x 1 spigot, which takes 4 turns over the 4 mm spigot. But the suspension cable passes through a Ø2 hole in the cap's lid and a Ø1.8 hole in the crown's floor, both off-centre at r 9.5. Turning the cap on would wind the cable round the grip inside the Ø21 pocket. Fitting the cable after the cap is impossible too. Its swaged ferrule sits under the crown's floor, in a counterbore in the hub, so it must be in place before the crown goes on. The assembly order in the note leaves the cable out.

findings.claim: The grip cannot be tightened once the cable is in, and the cable has to go in first (B1). The note says to use a thin-wall 15 mm socket down the pocket. But the cable runs up the same pocket, 0.10 mm from the drawn hex's corners, so no socket fits over the hex. The grip, which now clamps the crown to the hub and carries the fixture (S1), could be at most finger-tight. The real Lapp part is worse. Its hex is 16 mm across the flats and turned to Ø17.6, so it already touches the cable, and a 16 mm socket is wider than the Ø21 pocket.

In today's main build, nothing ties the hub to the cable that is now the default suspension. The fixture is meant to hang from the steel cable. But for today's top the cable is still drawn as a Ø5 fitting standing on the cap's top. The cap's 'two M3 into the crown' are not drawn. The crown only sits on the hub's neck. So the hub, shade and carrier are tied to nothing that the cable or the cap holds. The note's rule 8 (a ferrule in the neck) is true of A and B only. Round 2 flagged this gap (the skeptic's missed load-path item); it is now the default. The main BOM also contradicts itself: the cord row says the cord grips hold the fixture, the suspension row says the cable does.

findings.claim:
In A and B the cable's load still goes through the cord grip, not into the hub. The ferrule's counterbore is open at the top, so a pull on the cable presses the ferrule up against the crown's 1 mm floor. That floor is held to the hub only by the grip. So the whole fixture hangs on the grip's 5 mm of M12 x 1.5 in the hub. It is not 'cord strain only', and 'the fixture hangs from the hub' is true only through the grip.
Strength is ample: by my estimate about 25-30 kN to strip the thread, against about 16 N (64 N at four times). But the joint is not sound as a suspension anchor:
- A cable gland is not a structural fastener.
- The crown has nothing keying it to the hub.
- Unscrewing the cap turns the crown in the direction that loosens the grip.
- The notes' thermal pad under the crown would sit in the clamped joint and let it relax.
Suggest anchoring the ferrule in the hub itself and keying the crown.

findings.claim:
With the clamp ring screwed down to the shoulder, the squeeze is set by the acrylic's thickness at the crown. The parts and process for that are not in the build documents, and real sheet won't hold the tolerance.
- The note assumes four silicone rings of 1.3 or 1.5, two of them shims in the 1 mm air gaps. The CAD draws two rings, and every BOM lists 'Two moulded silicone rings (Shore 40, black, 1 mm)'. Built from the BOM, the ring seats with zero squeeze, or 2 mm of play if the air gaps close.
- The table's arithmetic reproduces exactly. Its premise does not: cast sheet held to ±10 % or ±5 %. ISO 7823-1 allows ±(0.4 + 0.1 t) on cast sheet, i.e. ±0.7 on 3 mm and ±1.0 on 6 mm (±17 to 23 %), before forming. On that, four 1.3 rings range from 23 % loose (1.2 mm of play) to 69 % squeeze in the worst case, -4 to 50 % RSS.
- So per-shade measurement and ring selection (the note's fallback) has to become a BOM and process item.
- The clamp's own note still says 'to a torque the shade maker sets' and 'two silicone rings'.
- No slip washer is drawn under the turning band.

findings.claim: The thread relief is not a usable run-out. The groove is 1.2 long at Ø94.5. That is shorter than one pitch of M96 x 1.5, and its floor sits above the thread's root (about Ø94.16). So the collar's thread cannot be cut fully up to the shoulder, and the last turn will be incomplete. The ring's thread has no lead-in chamfer, so the ring may jam before its face reaches the shoulder, which defeats the fixed height. A standard undercut for a 1.5 pitch is about 2.5-3.5 pitches long and cut below the root. These figures are from a DIN 76 excerpt and memory (UNVERIFIED in detail).

verdicts.reason:
Confirmed on my own build of the tip's sources (build123d 0.13.0 in my own venv). Output: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b84/eng-skeptic/out/geo.txt.
- The crown has no material in a Ø1.7 rod at (9.5, 0) through the floor, z 102.4-103.6.
- The cap has no material in a Ø1.9 rod at (9.5, 0) through the lid, and has material at (-9.5, 0).
- The hub tops out at z 102.5 with nothing over the Ø4.5 counterbore. The floor sits straight on the ferrule (crystal.py:488-494, :499, :507).
- The cap's Ø26 bore runs 4 mm onto the M26 x 1 spigot (:488, :493), so it takes 4 turns.
The lid hole is off the axis, and the grip and cord fill the axis. So turning the cap winds the cable round the grip; there is no way round this. With a free top end, the cap goes on only with the cable as a 4-turn helix round the grip and cap nut, not as drawn. The lid hole's final angle is not clocked either.
The Ø4 ferrule cannot pass the floor's Ø1.8 hole, so the cable has to go in before the crown. The order at top-redraw.md:36-39 has no cable step. Blocking is fair.

Confirmed (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b84/eng-skeptic/out/geo.txt):
- The exact grip-to-suspension distance is 0.100.
- The hex's corners are at 0/60/.../300 deg, one pointing at the cable.
- A socket tube of ID 17.6 over the drawn hex overlaps the cable by 10.8 / 25.1 / 34.0 mm3 at walls of 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5. It touches nothing else, crown or cap. So the cable alone stops any socket, whatever its brand OD.
The build order puts the cable in first: the cable before the crown, the grip through the crown's floor. An open-end or flare-nut spanner cannot get into a Ø21 pocket.
I downloaded Lapp's sheet myself from DigiKey's link (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b84/eng-skeptic/dl-lapp/DB53112005EN.pdf; same md5 as the reviewer's copy). It gives SW 16 and ØA 17.6, and its drawing shows ØA across the hex corners. So the real hex sweeps r 8.8, past the cable's r 8.75 (0.087 mm3 in my check).

Confirmed from the code:

- :472: the cap has only its Ø8 bore. The 'two M3' of :563 are not drawn.

So the cable pulls the ferrule into the floor, and only the grip's hex holds the floor down. The lamp hangs on the grip's 5 mm of M12 x 1.5 in the 6061. The tens-of-kN strength estimate against about 16 N is plausible.

- With the cable's own stiffness (my estimates, UNVERIFIED): EI of 400-5000 N mm2, a range for a 1.5 mm 7x7, gives 7.2-8.7 deg (A), 6.9-8.3 (B) and 3.6-4.2 (today). Even a solid 1.5 mm steel rod would give 4.6-4.8 deg (A, B) and 2.5 (today).
- What it looks like: the 200 mm rim sits 16-30 mm higher on one side in A and B, and 9-15 mm today.

So 'the fixture hangs from it; the cord beside it carries the 26 V only' cannot be true. That text is in bom.csv:21, topA/B bom.csv:22, crystal.py:503-504 and :570-572, and top-redraw.md:40.

AS NAMED, THE GRIP STOPS THE CAP GOING ON AND DOES NOT CLAMP THE CROWN. S2 gives the numbers but not this result.
- Lapp's part has 12 mm of thread (D) and is 32.5 mm overall.
- The hub is tapped only from z 97.5 to 102.6 (crystal.py:491). Below that is the Ø10 wire bore (:427), smaller than the root of an M12 x 1.5 (about 10.2). So the thread can go in only 6 mm: the 5 of tapping plus the 1 mm floor.
- The body's face then stops at about z 109.5, 6 mm above the floor, so nothing clamps the crown.
- Its top stands at about z 130.0, 5 mm into the cap's lid, whose underside is at z 125 (:493). The cap cannot seat.
The fix is easy (tap 12 deep), but the part as drawn and listed does not fit.

THE CAP NUT CANNOT BE TIGHTENED EITHER. The note's order needs 'its dome nut tightened' (top-redraw.md:38-39), in the same Ø21 pocket, with the cable 0.10 from the drawn grip. Lapp's drawing shows a second hex on the cap nut; its size is not listed separately. B2 covers only the body's hex, but the cord's strain relief depends on the cap nut.

THE CABLE BECOMES THE CROWN'S ONLY KEY. The floor's Ø1.8 hole sits straight over the hub's Ø4.5 counterbore, both at r 9.5 (crystal.py:490-492), and the ferrule's top bears on the floor. The joint allows about 0.4 mm of play (0.25 at the ferrule, 0.15 in the hole), which is about 2.4 deg at r 9.5. Past that, any turn of the crown on the neck side-loads and kinks the cable right at the swage's exit. That can happen when the grip's hex drags the floor as it is tightened, or from the cap's torque going on or off. That termination now carries the lamp. S1 says the crown is not keyed but not that the cable becomes the key.

THE PINS' BOM TEXT DOES NOT MATCH THE CAD. This is older than this round (since 367709bf89) and outside its diff, but it is on the bayonet.

A shade could not be fitted with pins bought from the BOM.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed independently. lamp_site.py:361-394 (origin/r32-lamps-final) calls part() only for clamp, crown, gland, hub, collar, white-disc, ring, pins, gaskets (when GASKETS=1), cord, carrier, stem and board. part() (:210-215) loads only the STL it is named, so the suspension is never loaded. crystal.py:505-507 and :570-572 make the cable the default in all three tops. bom.csv:21 moved it out of the options in 92dc7c25f5. In topA/topB, suspension.stl spans x 7.00-12.00 and z 99.50-726.00 (my reader). Today's lamp-site folder has no suspension.stl (top_tiers.py:20-22). The reviewer's UNVERIFIED side can be settled, and it does not change the outcome. strata/scene.py:321-322 imports STL with Blender's default axes and part() only moves it, so CAD +x is world +x. With HOUSE_CAM's right vector (0.901, 0.433), A's and B's cable falls 8.56 mm right of the cord's axis: 42 px on the crops, 24 px in the frames (8.56 mm left if the import were mirrored). The cable hides behind the cord only within 23.2 deg of the line of sight, and the camera is 64 deg away from it. Today's cable falls 4.96 mm right, and its Ø5 ferrule widens the right side of the cord to 7.5 mm for 9 mm above the cap.
